title: EventInput
description: One heraldo event as a sender posts it, envelope v1. The kind field picks the meaning of key and action. An input without kind is untyped: the server's ingest rules may type it, and it is stored as kind message when no rule matches. An explicit kind, message included, is final. The server owns id, received_at, cursor, hold and delivery: an input that sets any of them is rejected. The stored form, with those fields, is $defs/Event.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: One stored heraldo event, as the read API returns it: the sender's fields plus the server-owned fields id, received_at, cursor, hold, delivery and, on an incident, incident.

id.description: Server-assigned event id. Sortable by arrival.

received_at.description: When the server stored the event, RFC 3339.

cursor.description: The list cursor of this event, as a page's next_cursor gives it. A read cursor moved to it marks every event up to this one read; after and before take it too.

hold.description: Triage state the server keeps for the event.

delivery.description: What happened to the push on each device.

incident.description: On an incident event: the incident as it stood after this event.

state.description: open: not acked or resolved. acked: someone acknowledged it. resolved: it is over.

opened_at.description: When the incident opened, RFC 3339. A resolve with no earlier open opens and resolves at once.

resolved_at.description: When the incident resolved, RFC 3339. Set when state is resolved.

EventFields.description: The fields a sender sets. Shared by EventInput and Event; it does not close the object, so it is not used alone.

ts.description: When the event happened, RFC 3339. The server uses the arrival time when it is missing.

source.description: The sender, such as a service or job name. One thread and icon per source by default.

host.description: The machine the event is about. It can differ from the sender: a monitor on one machine reports about another. Status views group by host.

key.description: Groups related events: the incident, progress, check-in or status key. incident, progress, checkin and status need one. The server derives apns-collapse-id from a hash of the key, so the key may be longer than APNs allows.

summary.description: The one-line push text. A digest pushes the summary only. Without a summary, the push carries a truncated body.

body.description: Markdown. The server stores the full text; a push carries the summary or a truncated copy. The limit is 256 KiB; the server counts bytes, this schema counts characters.

thread.description: Notification thread. Maps to thread-id. Defaults to the source.

url.description: Opened when the notification is tapped.

icon.description: Icon for the source: an https URL, or the name of an icon in the server's registry (GET /v1/icons). Without it, the push uses the registry icon named after the source, when there is one.

sound.description: Push sound: "default", "none", or the name of a sound bundled with the app. Leave it out for the default.

tags.description: Free-form labels for rule matching, such as legacy Apprise tags.

dedup.description: Idempotency id chosen by the sender. The server drops a repeat with the same dedup within 24 hours and returns the first event. Set it when a sender may retry the same event.

expires_at.description: The event is stale after this time, RFC 3339. Maps to apns-expiration; views hide the event after it.

relevance.description: How relevant the event is next to others from the same app, 0 to 1. Maps to relevance-score.

KindRules.description: What each kind requires and allows. An untyped input, without kind, allows what message allows: no action, content or checkin.

Kind.description: What the event is. message: a one-off notice. incident: a problem with a lifecycle. digest: a batch summary. progress: a Live Activity. checkin: a job run, as with healthchecks.io. status: a named live value for widgets and the status view; it never sends an alert push, only a widget push. incident, progress, checkin and status need a key.

EventAction.description: Step within a kind. incident: open, update, ack, resolve. progress: start, update, end. checkin: start, success, fail, log. status: set, clear (required; set needs content). message and digest take none.

Level.description: Interruption level. Maps to the APNs interruption-level. Without the critical-alerts entitlement, the server sends critical as time-sensitive and records the downgrade in delivery.

Color.description: A hex color (#RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA) or a system color name.

Action.title: Action
Action.description: A button on a notification, Live Activity or widget. type open: the device opens url. type http: the device calls url with method, so it can reach hosts only the device sees, such as the LAN. type server: heraldo handles it; id names the server action (ack, resolve or mute) and url is not used.

id.description: Action id, unique within the event. For type server, the server action.

type.description: Who handles the tap: open and http run on the device, server runs on heraldo.

url.description: open: the page to open. http: the URL to call. Required for both; not allowed for server.

method.description: HTTP method for type http. Not allowed for other types.

foreground.description: Bring the app to the foreground when tapped.

LiveContent.title: LiveContent
LiveContent.description: What a Live Activity (kind progress) or widget (kind status) shows. On an update, a field left out keeps its value and a field set to null clears it.

symbol.description: SF Symbol name, such as printer.fill.

tint.description: Accent color: a hex color (#RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA) or a system color name.

steps.description: Step counter, such as layer 3 of 120. current should not exceed total; the server checks that.

ends_at.description: When the work is expected to end, RFC 3339. Absolute, so a late push does not shift it.

trailing.description: Short text on the trailing edge, such as an ETA.

status.description: Short state text, such as Printing or Paused.

button.description: One button on the activity or widget. Same shape as a notification action.

stale_after.description: Seconds after this update when the content counts as stale.

keep_for.description: On end: seconds the ended activity stays on screen.

Metric.title: Metric
Metric.description: One labelled value, such as Nozzle 215 °C.

value.description: The value as display text, such as 215 or 1.2k.

Checkin.title: Checkin
Checkin.description: Run details for kind checkin, in the shape of a healthchecks.io ping.

rid.description: Run id. Pairs a start with its success or fail, so the server can measure the run.

exit_code.description: The job's exit code. 0 counts as success, anything else as fail.

duration_ms.description: How long the run took, in milliseconds, when the sender measured it.

Schedule.title: Schedule
Schedule.description: When the check expects a ping. The server uses it only to create a check it does not know yet, as healthchecks.io does with ?create=1; after that the check's config lives on the server. Set period_s, or cron with an optional tz, not both.

cron.description: Cron expression for the expected pings.

tz.description: IANA time zone for cron, such as Europe/Madrid. Defaults to UTC.

grace_s.description: Seconds a ping may be late before the check fails.

max_runtime_s.description: Seconds a started run may take before the check fails.

Delivery.title: Delivery
Delivery.description: The outcome of the push on one device.

outcome.description: sent: APNs accepted the push. failed: APNs refused it; see error. skipped: a rule or device setting held it back.

at.description: When the server got the outcome, RFC 3339.

error.description: Why the push failed or was skipped. On a sent push, a note such as a downgraded level.
